title: Push or Pull? Picture Sort
students: Cut out 8 pictures of everyday actions (opening a door, kicking a ball, pulling a wagon) and glue each under Push or Pull.

title: Ramp Roll Race
students: Roll a ball down a low book ramp and a tall one, circle which rolled farther, and draw its path.

title: Which Way Will It Go?
students: Draw an arrow showing which way each of 6 pictured objects will move after a push or a pull.

title: Soft Push, Hard Push
students: Push a toy car gently and then hard, mark each stopping spot with tape, and draw both spots.

title: Bump! What Happens Next?
students: Look at 4 pictures of a ball about to hit a wall, a block or a pillow, and circle what happens next.

title: Change Its Direction
students: Tap a rolling ball sideways with a ruler 3 times and draw before and after arrows for each try.

title: Playground Pushes and Pulls
students: Find and circle 5 pushes and 5 pulls in a busy playground picture, then count each kind.

title: Stop the Marble Wall
students: Draw a block wall plan to stop a rolling marble, test it, and circle a happy or sad face for how it worked.

title: Pushes and Pulls Check-In
students: Circle push or pull for 6 pictures, draw arrows for 2 moving objects, and draw one strong push.

title: Sunny Spot, Shady Spot
students: Feel paper squares left in the sun and in the shade, then circle warm or cool for each spot.

title: Which Gets Warmest?
students: Leave black paper, white paper, sand and water in sunlight for an hour, feel each, and number them warmest to coolest.

title: Sun or Shade Maze
students: Maze: at each turn pick the warm or cool picture (sunny sidewalk, shady tree) to lead a lizard to the coolest rock.

title: Trees Make Shade
students: Draw the sun, a tree and its shadow, then draw a puppy resting in the coolest place.

title: Build a Shade for a Toy
students: Circle 2 materials from pictures (paper, foil, cloth, leaves) and draw a shade you will build for a toy animal.

title: Ice Cube Shade Test
students: Put an ice cube under your shade and one in the sun, draw both after 10 minutes, and circle which melted less.

title: Make My Shade Better
students: Draw one change that would make the shade work better and tell a partner why while the teacher writes it.

title: Sun and Shade Check-In
students: Circle the warmer place in 4 picture pairs, draw a shadow for one object, and circle the best shade material.

title: Living or Not? Cut and Sort
students: Cut out 10 pictures (rock, dog, tree, toy, bird, ball) and glue them under Living or Not Living.

title: Plant Needs, Animal Needs
students: Glue picture cards for water, light, food and air into a two-circle chart for plants and animals.

title: Bean Plant Watch
students: Draw the class bean plant every 3 days for 2 weeks and circle whether it got water and light.

title: Water or No Water?
students: Compare a watered cup of grass seed with a dry cup, draw both after a week, and circle the healthy one.

title: Feed the Animals Match
students: Match: draw lines from 6 animals to their foods, then circle the animals that eat only plants.

title: Bird Feeder Visitors
students: Tally birds and squirrels seen at a schoolyard feeder for 3 days and fill a picture graph square for each.

title: A Home Has What They Need
students: Draw water, food and shelter inside a rabbit's habitat box as the teacher reads each label.

title: Class Fish Care Plan
students: Draw what the class fish needs each day (food, clean water, light) and circle how often each is given.

title: Living Things Check-In
students: Circle the living things, match 4 animals to their food, and draw one thing every plant needs.

title: Weather Picture Words
students: Match 6 weather pictures (sunny, rainy, windy, cloudy, snowy, stormy) to their symbols, then draw today's weather.

title: Our Weather Calendar
students: Glue a weather symbol for each school day for a month and draw what to wear on one day.

title: Count the Weather Days
students: Count sunny, cloudy and rainy days from the class calendar, fill a picture graph, and circle the most common.

title: Wind Streamer Watch
students: Hang a paper streamer outside, draw how it moves on 3 days, and circle still, breezy or windy.

title: Dress for the Weather
students: Cut out clothing pictures and glue the right outfit on a child for a sunny, a rainy and a snowy day.

title: Four Seasons Sort
students: Sort 12 pictures (snowman, beach, falling leaves, flowers) into four season boxes.

title: Storm Safety Choices
students: Circle the safe choice in 4 pictures about thunder, lightning and heavy rain, and draw a safe place to wait.

title: Hot Day, Cold Day Thermometer
students: Shade a picture thermometer high for a hot day and low for a cold day, and draw clothes for each.

title: Weather Watch Check-In
students: Draw today's weather symbol, read a 5-day picture graph, and circle the safe choice in a storm.

title: Who Changed This Place?
students: Match 6 pictures of changes (beaver dam, ant hill, roots cracking a sidewalk) to the living thing that made each.

title: Nest Builders and Diggers
students: Draw how a bird changes a tree when building a nest and how a squirrel changes the ground.

title: Worm Jar Watch
students: Watch a class worm jar with sand and soil layers for a week and draw how the layers mix each day.

title: People Change Places Too
students: Sort 8 pictures of human changes (planting trees, littering, building a road) into Helps Nature or Hurts Nature.

title: Reuse, Recycle or Compost?
students: Cut out 9 pictures of lunch leftovers and wrappers and glue each into a Reuse, Recycle or Compost bin.

title: Our Class Earth Helper Plan
students: Draw one way the class can make less lunch trash and circle the things needed to do it.

title: Kindergarten Science Big Review
students: Circle a push, the warmer spot, what plants need, today's weather symbol and an animal changing its home.

title: Feel the Buzz
students: Hum with fingers on your throat and twang a ruler on a desk edge, then draw what moves when sound happens.

title: Dancing Rice Drum
students: Tap plastic wrap stretched over a bowl with rice on top, softly then loudly, and draw how high the rice jumps.

title: Rubber Band Box Guitar
students: Pluck tight and loose rubber bands stretched over an open box and circle which makes the higher sound.

title: What Vibrates Here?
students: Label the part that vibrates on a guitar, drum, bell and person singing, using a 4-word word bank.

title: Loud or Soft, High or Low
students: Sort 10 sound pictures (whisper, siren, bird, tuba, kitten) into a four-box grid of loud, soft, high and low.

title: Cup and String Phone
students: Build a cup phone, test it with the string tight and loose, and record whether a message was heard each time.

title: Signals That Talk to Us
students: Match 6 signals (fire alarm, school bell, whistle, car horn, crossing light) to what each tells people to do.

title: Design a Clean-Up Signal
students: Draw and label a device that uses sound or light to tell the class it is clean-up time, then test it.

title: Sound Words Draw It
students: Draw a picture for vibrate, pitch, loud and soft, and finish one sentence using vibrate.

title: Sound Check-In
students: Circle what vibrates in 4 pictures, sort 4 sounds as high or low, and draw one sound signal.

title: Peek in the Box
students: Look into a shoebox through a peephole with the lid closed and then with a flap open, and draw what you saw.

title: Will Light Shine Through?
students: Shine a flashlight at 8 materials (wax paper, foil, plastic wrap, cardboard) and sort them all, some or no light through.

title: Fix the Shadow Mistakes
students: Fix the mistakes in 5 shadow drawings (shadow on the wrong side, wrong shape) by crossing out and redrawing each one.

title: Mirror Bounce Path
students: Draw arrows showing how light from a flashlight bounces off a mirror to reach a paper star.

title: Mirror Maze Challenge
students: Use two small mirrors to bounce flashlight light onto a target, then draw the setup that worked.

title: Shadow Puppet Stage
students: Cut out an animal puppet, make its shadow on the wall, and draw how the shadow changes as it moves closer to the light.

title: Shadow Size Cube Graph
students: Measure a puppet's shadow in cubes at 3 distances from a flashlight and fill a bar graph.

title: Lights Out Story
students: Listen to a short story about a cat in a dark closet, circle why it could not see, and draw a fix.

title: Light and Shadow Check-In
students: Sort 6 materials by how much light passes, draw one shadow, and draw a mirror bounce arrow.

title: Plant Parts Label
students: Label root, stem, leaf, flower and seed on a bean plant from a word bank and draw what one part does.

title: Animal Parts, Animal Jobs
students: Match 8 animal parts (shell, claws, gills, beak, quills) to the job each does to help the animal survive.

title: Bird Beak Buffet
students: Pick up beans, rice and water with tweezers, a clothespin and a spoon, and tally which tool worked best for each food.

title: Spines, Shells and Thorns
students: Circle the body part that protects each of 6 plants and animals and tell a partner how it keeps them safe.

title: Ideas Copied from Nature
students: Listen to how burr hooks inspired hook-and-loop fasteners, then circle 3 other inventions copied from plants or animals.

title: Design Like a Turtle
students: Draw a helmet or backpack design that copies an animal part (shell, quills, webbed feet) and label the copied part.

title: Which Part Do We Eat?
students: Sort 8 pictured foods (carrot, celery, broccoli, sunflower seeds, lettuce) by the plant part we eat.

title: Parts Check-In
students: Label 4 plant parts, match 4 animal parts to their jobs, and draw one invention inspired by nature.

title: Baby and Grown-Up Match
students: Cut and glue 8 baby animals next to their parents, then circle one way each pair looks alike.

title: Puppies Like Their Parents
students: Compare a pictured dog family and draw 3 ways the puppies look like the parents and 2 ways they differ.

title: Leaf Line-Up
students: Collect 5 leaves from one tree, trace them, and circle how they are alike and how they are different.

title: How Animal Parents Help
students: Listen to short passages about penguins, kangaroos and elephants caring for young, then match each to its behavior.

title: Help the Baby Survive
students: For 5 pictured baby animals, circle what the parent does: feed, protect, keep warm or teach.

title: How Long Do Babies Stay?
students: Read a picture chart of how long 5 baby animals stay with their parents and circle the longest and shortest.

title: Seed to Sunflower
students: Draw a sunflower seed, sprout and grown plant in order, and circle what the young plant shares with its parent.

title: Families Check-In
students: Match 4 babies to parents, circle one parent behavior, and draw one way a young animal looks like its parent.

title: Where Is the Sun Now?
students: Draw the sun's place in the sky over the school at morning, noon and afternoon on one day.

title: Moon Shape Calendar
students: Draw the moon's shape each school day for 2 weeks from the class moon calendar and circle when it was round.

title: Moon Shapes in Order
students: Cut and glue 4 moon shape pictures in the order they appear, from full moon to new moon and back.

title: Why Stars Come Out at Night
students: Listen to a short passage about why we see stars only at night, then circle true or false for 4 sentences.

title: Daylight Hours Bar Graph
students: Fill bars for hours of daylight in 4 months from a class chart and circle the longest and shortest.

title: Winter Day, Summer Day
students: Compare a winter and a summer day by drawing when it gets dark, what we wear and how high the sun climbs.

title: Day and Night Color by Code
students: Color by code: decide if each numbered picture space (owl, sun, stars, rooster) is day or night and color it from the key.

title: Grade 1 Science Big Review
students: Answer mixed picture questions on what vibrates, what blocks light, a plant part's job, a parent behavior and moon shapes.

title: Material Detectives
students: Test 8 objects for hard or soft, bendy or stiff, and rough or smooth, and check boxes in a results chart.

title: Mystery Material Bag
students: Mystery object investigation: feel 4 hidden objects in a bag, record 3 properties each, and guess the material before peeking.

title: Best Material for the Job
students: Pick the best material for 5 jobs (umbrella, window, spoon, raincoat, pillow) and give one property as the reason.

title: Drip Drop Soak Test
students: Drip 10 drops of water on paper towel, cloth, foil and wax paper and record which soaked up the most.

title: Which Paper Holds the Most?
students: Read a bar graph of pennies 4 paper bridges held before bending and answer 5 questions about the strongest choice.

title: Material Riddles
students: Solve 8 riddles like "I am hard, clear and break easily" by naming the material, then write one riddle.

title: Property Word Maps
students: Make word maps for flexible, absorbent and transparent with a drawing, an example and a non-example.

title: Materials Check-In
students: Sort 6 objects by material, name a property for each, and choose the best material for a rain hat.

title: Block Build Remix
students: Build a shape from 10 blocks, take it apart, build a new object with the same pieces, and draw both.

title: Melt It, Cool It
students: Warm ice, butter and chocolate chips in a sunny spot, then cool them, and record which changes went back.

title: Can It Change Back?
students: Sort 10 pictured changes (melting ice, cooking an egg, freezing juice, burnt toast) into Can Go Back and Cannot.

title: Ice Cube Melt Race
students: Time ice cubes melting on a plate, in a cup and wrapped in cloth, then make a bar graph.

title: Juice Pop Change Chain
students: Draw 4 steps of juice freezing into a pop and melting again, with arrows labeled heating and cooling.

title: Kitchen Change Detectives
students: Read 5 kitchen scenes (toast, melted cheese, frozen pops, pancakes, ice) and tell if heating or cooling caused each and if it reverses.

title: Heating and Cooling Check-In
students: Sort 6 changes as reversible or not, label heating or cooling, and draw one object rebuilt from the same pieces.

title: Fair Test for Beans
students: Plan a test with 4 bean cups (water and light, water only, light only, neither) and predict each result.

title: Bean Plant Growth Log
students: Measure 4 bean plants in cubes every 3 days for 3 weeks and draw any color changes.

title: Bean Results Bar Graph
students: Graph final plant heights from the class bean test and write which need mattered most.

title: Seeds on the Move
students: Examine 6 seeds (burr, maple wing, dandelion, acorn) and test whether each travels by blowing, sticking or rolling.

title: Fuzzy Bee Pollinator Model
students: Use a pom-pom bee to visit 3 paper flowers dusted with chalk powder and draw how the powder moved.

title: Flower Parts and Pollen
students: Label petal, stem, pollen and seed on a flower, then draw arrows showing a bee carrying pollen between flowers.

title: Plant Needs Check-In
students: Circle what a plant needs, match 4 seeds to how they travel, and explain a bee's job in one sentence.

title: Hula Hoop Life Count
students: Count kinds of plants and animals inside a hula hoop on grass and on pavement, recording tallies for each.

title: Which Spot Has More Life?
students: Graph the kinds of living things found in 2 schoolyard spots and explain which has more variety.

title: Pond or Desert?
students: Compare a pond and a desert habitat in a T-chart listing 4 plants, 4 animals and the water each has.

title: One Tree, Many Neighbors
students: Read a short passage about a rainforest tree home to many living things, then answer 5 questions.

title: Who Lives Here?
students: Cut and glue 12 plants and animals into ocean, forest, desert and arctic habitat boxes.

title: Could It Live There?
students: Decide if 5 animals could survive in a new habitat and explain using what each animal needs.

title: Habitat Maze Review
students: Maze review: choose the animal that fits each habitat at every turn to reach the exit, then explain one choice.

title: Fast or Slow Earth Changes
students: Sort 10 events (earthquake, canyon carving, volcano, landslide, river bending) into Fast and Slow.

title: Sand Hill Rainstorm
students: Pour water slowly down a sand hill in a pan and draw the land before and after, labeling where sand moved.

title: Save the Sand Hill
students: Design a way to keep a sand hill from washing away (rocks, sticks, plastic wrap), test it, and compare with a bare hill.

title: Wind Moves the Land
students: Wearing goggles, blow through a straw across a sand tray, then add a craft stick fence and draw how the pattern changes.

title: Minutes to Millions of Years
students: Place 6 events (rockfall, flood, mountain wearing down, canyon forming) on a time strip from minutes to millions of years.

title: Landforms Check-In
students: Label 4 changes fast or slow, draw how water moved sand, and pick the best way to stop erosion.

title: Land and Water Word Pictures
students: Draw and label island, lake, river, mountain, valley and ocean, and write one sentence about each.

title: Bird's-Eye Landform Map
students: Draw a bird's-eye map of a model landscape with a key for hill, lake, river and plain.

title: Find the Water
students: On a simple map of the United States, circle 2 oceans, 2 lakes and 2 rivers, and mark which hold salt water.

title: Where Is Water Frozen?
students: Read about glaciers and ice caps, then answer questions about where Earth's water is solid, liquid and salty.

title: Water on Earth Picture Graph
students: Read a 100-square picture graph of ocean, ice and fresh water and answer 4 questions about how much is salty.

title: Island Treasure Map
students: Follow 6 directions using landform words to draw a treasure map of an island with a river, hill and lake.

title: Grade 2 Science Big Review
students: Answer mixed questions on material properties, reversible changes, plant needs, habitats, fast and slow changes and map features.

title: Tug-of-War Arrows
students: Draw force arrows on 6 tug-of-war and pushing pictures, sizing them by strength, and label each balanced or unbalanced.

title: Balanced or Not? Task Strips
students: Task-card strips: decide if forces are balanced on 8 cut strips (book on a table, kicked ball, stuck wagon) and predict the motion.

title: Ruler Seesaw Balance
students: Balance a ruler on a pencil with pennies at different distances and record which setups balance and which tip.

title: Pendulum Pattern Lab
students: Swing a washer pendulum, count swings in 15 seconds for 3 string lengths, and predict the count for a fourth length.

title: Pendulum Swing Graph
students: Graph class pendulum data for each string length and describe the pattern you could use to predict the next swing.

title: Playground Forces
students: Explain the forces on a swing, slide, seesaw and merry-go-round using balanced, unbalanced, push and pull.

title: Forces Check-In
students: Draw arrows for 3 force scenes, label each balanced or unbalanced, and use a motion pattern to make a prediction.

title: Will the Magnet Pick It Up?
students: Predict, then test 10 classroom objects with a magnet and sort them into attracted and not attracted.

title: Paper Clips Through Cardboard
students: Count how many paper clips a magnet holds through 0, 1, 2 and 3 cardboard sheets and graph the results.

title: Balloon Static Tricks
students: Rub a balloon on wool, hold it near paper bits, a thin stream of water and another balloon, and record what happens.

title: Attract or Repel?
students: Label poles on 6 pairs of bar magnets and draw arrows showing whether each pair attracts or repels.

title: Magnet Problem Solvers
students: Design a magnet fix for 3 problems (a cabinet door that swings open, spilled pins, a flapping bag) and sketch each.

title: Hidden Poles Logic
students: Use clues about which ends attract or repel to figure out the hidden poles on 4 taped-over magnets.

title: Magnets Check-In
students: Predict attract or repel for 4 pairs, explain the paper clip graph, and describe one static electricity effect.

title: Butterfly and Frog Cycles
students: Draw and label the 4 stages of a butterfly and a frog life cycle and circle the stages both share.

title: Bean in a Bag Journal
students: Watch a bean sprout in a clear bag taped to a window for 2 weeks, drawing and dating each new stage.

title: Chicken, Frog, Bean Compare
students: Fill a 3-column chart of birth, growth, reproduction and death for a chicken, a frog and a bean plant.

title: Mealworm Watch
students: Observe mealworms in bran for 4 weeks, recording each one's stage, length and behavior to describe its life cycle.

title: How Long to Grow Up?
students: Read a bar graph of life spans for 6 animals and answer questions comparing their life cycles.

title: Life Cycle Crossword
students: Crossword with real clues on 12 life cycle words (larva, pupa, tadpole, seedling), then order one scrambled cycle.

title: Why Wolves Hunt Together
students: Read a short passage about a wolf pack, then answer questions about how the group helps each member survive.

title: Group Jobs Chart
students: Fill a chart for ants, bees, a fish school and an elephant herd showing what the group does and how it helps.

title: Safety in a School of Fish
students: Read a table of how many fish a predator caught from schools of different sizes and make a claim from the data.

title: Alone or in a Group?
students: Use a claim, evidence and reasoning frame to argue whether a meerkat survives better alone or in a group.

title: Traits from Parents
students: Circle the inherited traits in 6 animal family pictures and write which trait each offspring shares with a parent.

title: Kitten Litter Trait Tally
students: Tally fur color, eye color and tail length for a pictured litter of 8 kittens and graph one trait.

title: Born With It or Shaped by Where It Lives?
students: Sort 10 traits (fur color, a dog's tricks, a plant leaning to light, beak shape) into inherited or environment-influenced.

title: Plants in Sun and Shade
students: Compare the same kind of plant grown in sun and shade, measure height and leaf color, and explain the difference.

title: Lima Bean Line Plot
students: Measure 20 lima beans in millimeters, make a line plot, and describe how individuals of one kind vary.

title: Beetle Colors Survive
students: Decide which of 4 beetle colors survives best on dark bark, light sand and green leaves and explain why.

title: Traits and Groups Check-In
students: Sort 6 traits as inherited or environmental, read a variation line plot, and explain one benefit of living in a group.

title: Fossil Clue Cards
students: Mystery investigation: read 6 fossil clue cards (fish in desert rock, palm leaves in Antarctica) and infer what each place was once like.

title: Make a Fossil Imprint
students: Press a shell or leaf into clay, trade with a partner, and identify their organism from the imprint alone.

title: Fossils in the Layers
students: Label 4 rock layers with their fossils, order them oldest to newest, and name the environment each layer shows.

title: When the Pond Dries Up
students: For 3 habitat changes (drought, new road, flood), decide which organisms survive, move away or die, and explain.

title: Pick the Best Habitat Fix
students: Compare 2 solutions for frogs cut off by a new road and write a claim about which works better.

title: Town Weather Table
students: Graph a month of daily high temperatures and rainfall for one town and describe the pattern.

title: Climate Around the World
students: Use a world climate map to compare 4 cities and write which is hot and wet, cold and dry, and so on.

title: Bottle Rain Gauge
students: Build a rain gauge from a clear bottle, mark it in centimeters, and record rainfall for 2 weeks.

title: Seasons in Two Cities
students: Make a bar graph of average temperatures by season for 2 cities and predict the weather in each next season.

title: Storm-Ready Designs
students: Evaluate 3 designs that reduce weather hazards (levee, lightning rod, storm shutters) and match each to its hazard.

title: Grade 3 Science Big Review
students: Answer mixed questions on forces, magnets, life cycles, groups, traits, fossils and reading a weather graph.

title: Ramp Height Cup Crash
students: Roll a ball from 3 ramp heights into a paper cup and measure how far the cup slides each time.

title: Speed and Energy Graph
students: Graph cup-slide distance against ramp height from class data and write a claim linking speed and energy.

title: Collision Energy Arrows
students: Draw energy arrows for 4 collisions (bowling, billiards, bumper cars, hammer on nail) and label sound, heat and motion.

title: Marble Line Crash
students: Roll one marble into a line of marbles in a ruler groove at slow and fast speeds and record how many move out.

title: Fix the Energy Mistakes
students: Fix the mistakes: find and correct the wrong energy claim in 10 short scenarios about sound, light, heat and motion.

title: Energy Change Chains
students: Draw energy conversion chains for 5 devices (flashlight, fan, toaster, wind-up toy, solar calculator).

title: Light the Bulb Circuits
students: Build a circuit with a battery, wire and bulb, draw 2 working and 2 non-working setups, and explain the difference.

title: Rubber Band Car Plan
students: Plan a rubber band car with a labeled sketch, a materials list, and 2 criteria for success.

title: Rubber Band Car Test Log
students: Test the car 3 times at 2 winding amounts, record distances, and choose one change to improve it.

title: Which Car Design Wins?
students: Compare a table of 4 teams' car distances, costs and materials, and recommend one design with reasons.

title: Energy Check-In
students: Explain energy in 2 collisions, draw one conversion chain, and use test data to pick a better design.

title: Wave Parts Label
students: Label crest, trough, wavelength and amplitude on 3 wave drawings and tell which has the biggest amplitude.

title: Coiled Spring Waves
students: Make waves on a coiled spring toy, change how hard and fast you shake it, and sketch amplitude and wavelength.

title: Waves Move Energy, Not Water
students: Read about a duck bobbing on pond waves and answer why it does not travel along with the wave.

title: Flashlight Code Messages
students: Decode and encode messages with a blink code key, then explain how patterns can carry information.

title: Inside and Outside Parts
students: Label external and internal structures of a fish and a sunflower and tell the job of each.

title: Animal Super Senses
students: Fill a chart for 5 animals showing a sense organ, what it detects, and how the animal uses that information.

title: How We See a Book
students: Draw arrows showing light from a lamp bouncing off a book into the eye, and number each step.

title: Ruler Drop Reaction
students: Catch a dropped ruler 5 times with each hand, record the distances, and explain how senses and the brain work together.

title: Cactus Survival Argument
students: Write a claim, evidence and reasoning paragraph about how 2 cactus structures help it survive in the desert.

title: Waves and Senses Check-In
students: Label a wave, decode a short signal, and explain the path of light from an object to the eye.

title: Read the Rock Layers
students: Number 5 rock layers with fossils from oldest to youngest and explain how the environment changed.

title: Layer Cup Model
students: Pour sand, soil and gravel in turns into a clear cup of water, then sketch and describe the layers that settle.

title: Canyon Wall Clues
students: Use a canyon wall diagram with a shell layer and a fern layer to tell the area's history in 3 steps.

title: Rock Layer Order Puzzle
students: Use clues about fossils, a cutting river and a tilted layer to put 6 events in the right order.

title: A Place Through Time
students: Order 6 stages from rock layers (shallow sea, swamp, desert, river cutting) on a timeline with a sketch for each.

title: Shake the Sugar Cubes
students: Shake sugar cubes in a jar for 1, 2 and 3 minutes and record how much they round off and crumble.

title: Weathering or Erosion Maze
students: Maze: at each turn decide if a scene shows weathering or erosion; correct answers lead a raindrop to the sea.

title: Ice Wedge Test
students: Freeze a small capped plastic tube filled with water and record what the ice did to the cap overnight.

title: Slope and Erosion Graph
students: Graph class data of sand moved at 3 stream table slopes and explain how slope changes erosion.

title: Roots That Crack and Hold
students: Explain from 3 described scenes how plant roots can both break rock and hold soil in place.

title: Rocks and Weathering Check-In
students: Order 3 rock layers, sort 4 scenes as weathering or erosion, and explain one slope graph result.

title: Ring of Fire Map
students: Mark 10 volcanoes and 10 earthquakes from a table on a world map and describe the pattern you see.

title: Ocean Floor Profile
students: Plot depths from a ship's sounding table to draw the ocean floor and find a trench and a ridge.

title: Mountains and Trenches Map
students: Use a relief map to locate 4 mountain ranges and 2 ocean trenches and note what each lies near.

title: Where Should the Town Go?
students: Use hazard maps to pick the safest of 3 town sites and justify the choice with map evidence.

title: Renewable or Not?
students: Sort 10 energy sources and fill a chart with where each comes from and one effect on the environment.

title: Power for a Windy Town
students: Compare coal, wind, solar and water power in a pros and cons table, then choose one for a windy coastal town.

title: Shake Table Towers
students: Build a tower of straws and tape, shake it on a tray, and test 2 changes that help it stay standing.

title: Flood Barrier Plan
students: Design a barrier for a riverside town, list materials, and explain how to test it in a sand tray.

title: Grade 4 Science Big Review
students: Answer mixed questions on energy transfer, waves, senses, rock layers, erosion, map patterns and hazard designs.

title: Where Did the Salt Go?
students: Dissolve salt in water, let drops evaporate on dark paper, and explain the crystals that appear using particles.

title: Dry Towel Under Water
students: Push an upside-down cup with a paper towel inside into water and explain why the towel stays dry.

title: Particle Model Drawings
students: Draw particle models of sugar before and after dissolving and of air in a syringe before and after squeezing.

title: Mass Before and After
students: Weigh water and salt separately and together after dissolving to test whether total mass stays the same.

title: Conservation Data Check
students: Analyze a table of masses before and after 5 changes (melting, dissolving, fizzing in a sealed bag) and explain.

title: Mystery Powder Tests
